context.requirement_text: REQ-204 acceptance criteria: (AC1) non-https scheme rejected; (AC2) 5 private-range rejections (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, 10.0.0.5, 172.16.0.5, 192.168.0.5); (AC3) legitimate https target succeeds; (AC4) DNS rebinding test in deliver/3; (AC5) no-redirect regression; (AC6) INV-9 added; (AC7) moduledoc ranges; (AC8) mix test passes; (AC9) no scope creep. ac_coverage.AC5: PASS — webhooks_test.exs REQ-204 AC5: File.read! on lib/letflow/webhooks.ex + two refute assertions (~r/autoredirect.*true/i and ~r/follow_redirect.*true/i). Source-assertion pattern present and correct.

additional_checks.skip_tags: None found in url_validator_test.exs or webhooks_test.exs
additional_checks.dns_injection: All hostname-based unit tests in url_validator_test.exs use injected resolver (validate/2 arity). IP-literal tests use validate/1 safely (check_ip_literal/1 short-circuits before DNS). No real DNS calls in unit tests.
additional_checks.test_independence: Each describe block that needs DB provisions its own tenant via provisioned_tenant/1. No cross-test ordering dependency.
additional_checks.application_get_env_bypass: ACCEPTABLE. The bypass (Application.put_env(:letflow, :webhook_ssrf_validation_enabled, false)) is confined to webhooks_delivery_test.exs (REQ-183 tests) in a setup/on_exit pair that is properly restored. The REQ-204 tests in webhooks_test.exs do NOT disable SSRF validation — AC4 in particular proves validation is active during deliver/3 (the test would pass through rather than fail without it). The bypass is a test-infrastructure necessity for REQ-183's local-server tests, not a coverage hole for REQ-204.
